what_is_wrong: Child entity has no RLS at all, so every logged-in user (parent, teacher, role=user) can read, create, update and delete every child record, including medical_notes, allergies, emergency_contacts, doctor_phone, date_of_birth and full_name.
how_you_saw_it: base44/entities/Child.jsonc has no "rls" key (grep -L '"rls"' base44/entities/*); the fields are listed in Child.jsonc properties
proposed_fix: Add RLS to Child. read: super_admin/admin, school_admin where data.school_id={{user.data.school_id}}, teacher where data.school_id={{user.data.school_id}}, parent where data.parent_user_ids contains {{user.id}}. create/update/delete: admin, super_admin, school_admin (same school) only.

what_is_wrong: TeacherNote has no RLS, so any logged-in user, including parents, can read and edit every teacher's notes about children.
how_you_saw_it: base44/entities/TeacherNote.jsonc has no rls block
proposed_fix: Add RLS so a note can be read and written only by its creator, admins, and school_admin/teacher of the same school_id. Parents get no access.

what_is_wrong: read is {} (open to all), so any logged-in user can list every parent-teacher message for every child and family. create/update allow every role, including 'user'.
how_you_saw_it: base44/entities/ParentMessage.jsonc:101 rls.read = {}; create/update $or lists all 6 roles
proposed_fix: read: sender (created_by_id), parents where child is theirs (store parent_user_ids on the message), staff of same school_id, admins. update: the sender only. Remove role 'user' from create.

page_or_entity: ParentObservation, ChildGrowthRecord, ChildMilestoneObservation, ChildPortfolioEntry, FamilyEcho, WeeklyGrowthReport
what_is_wrong: read is {} on all of these, so any logged-in user can read every child's growth, portfolio, milestone and family data across all schools. create/update are granted to every role, including parent and 'user'. A parent can therefore edit any other child's records.
how_you_saw_it: ParentObservation.jsonc:62, ChildGrowthRecord.jsonc:53, ChildMilestoneObservation.jsonc:102, ChildPortfolioEntry.jsonc:124, FamilyEcho.jsonc:72, WeeklyGrowthReport.jsonc:115: rls.read = {}
proposed_fix: Scope read and update to: admins; staff where data.school_id={{user.data.school_id}}; parents where data.parent_user_id={{user.id}} or data.child_id is in the user's child_ids (denormalise parent_user_ids onto each row if needed).

what_is_wrong: ParentNotification: read {} and update {} mean anyone can read and edit any family's notifications. SpecialTimeSession: read {} means anyone can read every family's special-time logs.
how_you_saw_it: ParentNotification.jsonc:94 read {} update {}; SpecialTimeSession.jsonc:34 read {}
proposed_fix: read/update: data.parent_user_id={{user.id}} (or created_by_id) plus admins.

page_or_entity: Classroom, School, ParentDashboardSnapshot, ParentSubscriptionPreference, SavedQuestion, ActivityCompletion, AIContentLog, Printable
what_is_wrong: None of these have RLS, so any user can write to them. School and Classroom can be created, edited or deleted by a parent or teacher. ParentDashboardSnapshot holds per-parent data and is readable by everyone.
how_you_saw_it: grep -L rls base44/entities/* lists these files
proposed_fix: School/Classroom: write limited to admin, super_admin, and school_admin of the same school. ParentDashboardSnapshot/ParentSubscriptionPreference/SavedQuestion: read/write limited to the owner (parent_user_id / user_id / created_by_id) plus admins.

what_is_wrong: No role check on the route (RoleRouteGuard only covers admin prefixes) or in the page. A parent or role=user who types /children sees every Child plus TeacherMessagesInbox, FamilyEchoesPanel and ParentObservationsInbox for all families.
how_you_saw_it: src/App.jsx:293; src/pages/ChildrenNotes.jsx:16 base44.entities.Child.list() with no filter; src/components/layout/RoleRouteGuard.jsx:7-17 prefix list has no /children
proposed_fix: Add a staff-only guard (teacher, school_admin, admin, super_admin) in RoleRouteGuard and filter Child by classroom/school. The real protection is the entity RLS in R-01..R-04.

what_is_wrong: No role check. A parent, teacher or role=user can open /classrooms and use Add/Edit/Delete Classroom, and the Classroom entity has no RLS. The page also lists all Users.
how_you_saw_it: src/App.jsx:251,253; src/pages/Classrooms.jsx:59,69 'Add Classroom' button not gated; ClassroomDialog.jsx:62-79 create/update/delete
proposed_fix: Add /classrooms and /age-groups to a staff-admin list (admin, super_admin, school_admin) in RoleRouteGuard, and add RLS to Classroom and AgeGroup.

what_is_wrong: Page loads Child.list(1000) and shows every child to any role. Only the 'Enrol child' button is gated (canEnroll). Teachers and parents see all children in all schools.
how_you_saw_it: src/App.jsx:252; src/pages/Enrollment.jsx:27 canEnroll, :36 Child.list; filtering only applies when role==='school_admin' (:62,:88)
proposed_fix: Guard the route for school_admin/admin/super_admin. Rely on Child RLS (R-01).

what_is_wrong: Explicitly exempted from the admin guard as 'open to any authenticated user', so parents and role=user can open admin upload tools that write Printable/Song records.
how_you_saw_it: src/components/layout/RoleRouteGuard.jsx:38-40 isOpenInternalTool; pages have no role check
proposed_fix: Remove the isOpenInternalTool exemption, or restrict it to staff roles.

what_is_wrong: Staff pages are reachable by parents and role=user by URL. /pro-studio has no role check and can update Song records (approve lyrics, change pro_tier). /ai-assistant lets any role run LLM generation. Reports and policies render for any role.
how_you_saw_it: src/App.jsx:278,291,292,300,353; src/pages/ProStudio.jsx:74,92,112 Song.update with no role check; RoleRouteGuard prefix list does not include these
proposed_fix: In RoleRouteGuard, send role=parent to /parent for every AppShell route except '/' redirects. Add a STAFF_ONLY check (teacher, school_admin, admin, super_admin) for the rest, and an admin check for /pro-studio.

what_is_wrong: isAdminLike() accepts only super_admin and admin, so school_admin is redirected away from /schools, /users, /kasvunpolku/admin, /network, /curriculum-canvas, /bulk-generation and /admin/music-room, even though all of these are in schoolAdminNav. Teachers are redirected from /kasvunpolku/admin, which is in teacherNav and allowed by KasvunpolkuControl. These are broken nav links.
how_you_saw_it: RoleRouteGuard.jsx:19-21 isAdminLike, :42 redirect; Sidebar.jsx:78-106 schoolAdminNav, :114 teacherNav includes /kasvunpolku/admin; KasvunpolkuControl.jsx:35 allows school_admin and teacher; UserManagement.jsx:32 canManage includes school_admin
proposed_fix: Replace the single prefix list with a per-prefix role map, e.g. {'/users':[admin,super_admin,school_admin], '/schools':[...,school_admin], '/kasvunpolku/admin':[...,school_admin,teacher], '/admin/':[admin,super_admin]}.

what_is_wrong: This admin control panel is mounted inside ParentGuard, so it is reachable by parents. The page's own check (allowed = super_admin/admin/school_admin/teacher) redirects a parent to '/', so no data is exposed today. The route is still dead and misleading: ParentGuard blocks teachers and school_admins, so only admins can use it.
how_you_saw_it: src/App.jsx:244; src/pages/KasvunpolkuControl.jsx:35-36,89 'if (!isAuthorised) return <Navigate to="/" />'
proposed_fix: Delete the /parent/admin route (admins already have /kasvunpolku/admin and /admin/kasvunpolku).

what_is_wrong: The guard applies only when role is truthy ('role && !isAdminLike'). A user with an empty or undefined role passes into every admin page. Sidebar also defaults a missing role to 'teacher'.
how_you_saw_it: RoleRouteGuard.jsx:42; Sidebar.jsx:165 'user?.role || teacher'
proposed_fix: Fail closed: treat a missing role as 'user' and block admin routes (if (isAdminRoute && !isAdminLike(role))).

what_is_wrong: 4 of 12 users have role 'user'. The sidebar shows them teacherNav (default branch), and RLS 'create/update' lists include 'user', so unassigned accounts get teacher-level write access to child records.
how_you_saw_it: query_entities User fields [role]: super_admin 2, teacher 3, parent 2, school_admin 1, user 4; Sidebar.jsx:157 default: teacherNav; e.g. ChildGrowthRecord.jsonc:53 create includes role user
proposed_fix: Give role=user a minimal nav (no child data). Remove 'user' from child-data create/update RLS. Assign real roles to the 4 accounts.

what_is_wrong: The only school_admin has no school_id. School-scoped filters (Enrollment.jsx:62, BackgroundJob RLS data.school_id={{user.data.school_id}}) will show them nothing or behave unexpectedly.
how_you_saw_it: query_entities User: school_admin record has no school_id field
proposed_fix: Set school_id on that user. Make UserManagement require school_id when the role is school_admin.

what_is_wrong: Correctly limited to real role super_admin/admin (isSuperAdmin), audit-logged to ImpersonationEvent (RLS admin-only). Two issues: the name says 'super admin' but plain 'admin' can also impersonate. It is UI-only: pages that read useAuth().user (KasvunpolkuControl, ChildrenNotes, Reports, BackgroundJobs) still render the admin's view, and ReadOnlyGuard only blocks buttons whose text matches write verbs, so writes run with the admin's JWT.
how_you_saw_it: src/lib/ImpersonationContext.jsx:28 isSuperAdmin = super_admin||admin; ViewAsPill.jsx:52; ReadOnlyGuard.jsx:6-17 text-matching; pages use useAuth not useImpersonation (e.g. ChildrenNotes.jsx:11)
proposed_fix: Decide whether 'admin' should impersonate; if not, change line 28 to super_admin only. Make pages read effectiveUser from useImpersonation(), and block writes centrally (e.g. wrap base44 entity writes when readOnly).

what_is_wrong: Automation handler with no auth check. It trusts the request body (event, data) and uses asServiceRole to email teachers, school admins or linked parents, with an attacker-supplied sender_name and body. Anyone who invokes the function directly can send platform-branded emails to any child's parents (phishing).
how_you_saw_it: base44/functions/onParentMessageCreated/entry.ts:12-28 reads data from req.json(); :87 asServiceRole.integrations.Core.SendEmail; no auth.me()/secret check
proposed_fix: At the top, reject unless the caller is the automation (check a shared secret header or that auth.me() is null/service). Re-load the ParentMessage by event.entity_id via asServiceRole instead of trusting the body.

what_is_wrong: Automation handlers with no caller check that trust body data and write with asServiceRole. A forged call can create ChildMilestoneObservations and parent updates for arbitrary children, overwrite ParentDashboardSnapshots and ParentNotifications, and clone the whole policy suite for any school_id (duplicates).
how_you_saw_it: functions/onActivityCompleted/entry.ts:17-153; onParentActivityCompletion/entry.ts:10-67; onParentMilestoneObserved/entry.ts:14-41; onSchoolCreatedClonePolicies/entry.ts:7-69 (no auth.me, no secret)
proposed_fix: Same fix as R-18: verify the automation origin (secret) and re-read the entity by event.entity_id with the service role instead of using body.data.

what_is_wrong: Scheduled jobs with no auth check that anyone can invoke. During the matching hour, repeated calls queue duplicate ParentNotifications for every parent.
how_you_saw_it: functions/sendWeeklySummaryNotifications/entry.ts:11-55 (only an hour check); sendWeeklyVoiceNote/entry.ts:29-59
proposed_fix: Require the scheduler secret or an admin caller, and dedupe per parent per week.

what_is_wrong: auth.me() is optional (errors are swallowed and there is no 401). An anonymous or any-role caller can trigger LLM generation and PDF upload, and overwrite any Printable record via asServiceRole (cost abuse and content tampering).
how_you_saw_it: functions/generatePrintable/entry.ts:37-45 'try { user = await base44.auth.me(); } catch (_) {}' then asServiceRole InvokeLLM :76, Printable.update :225
proposed_fix: Require an authenticated staff/admin user: if (!user || ![admin,super_admin,school_admin,teacher].includes(user.role)) return 403.

page_or_entity: exportPolicyToPDF, exportPolicyToWord, exportCurriculumOutline, charterHealthMetrics, generateChapterAudio, generateBookChapterAudio, generateForestSchoolImage, generateSongPracticeSheet, validateAudioAgainstCharter
what_is_wrong: These check login only (401), not role. A parent or role=user can run paid generation (audio, images) and export any school's policy documents via asServiceRole.
how_you_saw_it: grep of base44/functions/*/entry.ts: asServiceRole used and auth.me() present but no role/403 check (e.g. exportPolicyToPDF/entry.ts:26-43)
proposed_fix: Add a role check for staff/admin; for policy exports also check doc.school_id === user.school_id unless admin.
